src.name: Wikipedia · Banksy
src.q: Banksy reportedly lived in Easton, Bristol, during the late 1990s, before moving to London around 2000.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Banksy
notes.q: In January 2011, Banksy published the original storyboard on his website.

src.name: Wikipedia · Banksy
src.q: In March 2010, a modified version of the work Forgive Us Our Trespassing–a kneeling boy with a spray-painted halo–was displayed at London Bridge Station on a poster.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Banksy
notes.q: On 18 February 2013, BBC News reported that a recent Banksy mural, known as the Slave Labour mural portraying a young child sewing Union Flag bunting (created around the time of the Diamond Jubilee of Elizabeth II), had been removed from the side of a Poundland store in Wood Green, north London, and soon appeared for sale in a catalogue of the US auction site Fine Art Auctions Miami.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Banksy
notes.q: On 1 October 2013, Banksy began a one-month "show on the streets of New York [City]", for which he opened a separate website and granted an interview to The Village Voice via his publicist.

src.name: Wikipedia · Banksy
src.q: In May 2012 his Parachuting Rat, painted in Melbourne in the late 1990s, was accidentally destroyed by plumbers installing new pipes.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Banksy
notes.q: In June 2017, DJ Goldie referred to Banksy as "Rob" in an interview for a podcast.

src.name: Wikipedia · Banksy
src.q: In May 2017, Banksy claimed the authorship of a giant Brexit mural, painted on a house in Dover (Kent).
